sources.name: AP Elections API
sources.cost: No public price found. Third-party sources (archived python-elections repo) say it is paid and sales-gated; an aggregator (apis.io) calls it freemium with no trial (unverified). Typically enterprise or newsroom pricing.
sources.latency: Not stated in the sources I could read. In practice AP is the main source for election-night calls. Quota is per-minute and set per key.
sources.granularity: National, state, county, and precinct-level reporting units, per the 2016 developer guide.
sources.verified_live: Portal page returns HTTP 200. api.ap.org/v2/elections returns 403, which means a key is required. WebFetch was blocked for developer.ap.org, so I could not read pricing or access terms.
sources.notes: The API Explorer needs an API key, and keys are issued by AP Customer Support rather than self-registered. An individual almost certainly cannot buy access tonight. Anecdotal reports say it is for news organizations only.

sources.name: Decision Desk HQ Results API (v4/v5)
sources.cost: No published price. Contact sales. The DDHQ site says to contact them for API or embed delivery. Broadcast license is a separate product with no dollar amount published. DDHQ Enterprise (a branded Votes portal) is also quote-only.
sources.latency: Not stated. Docs mention a vote-history endpoint that records every vote update. No timing is given.
sources.granularity: Race-level data, plus congress control, electoral college, and balance-of-power endpoints. Also polling averages, vote history, and forecast data. Precinct depth is not confirmed.
sources.verified_live: Docs site is up (HTTP 200 after redirects). The API itself was not probed because credentials are required.
sources.notes: A production-identical Testing Environment exists, but access instructions were not found. The free DDHQ Votes website (decisiondeskhq.com) is a human-readable fallback, but there is no free API tier that I could confirm. An individual probably has to go through sales.
sources.auth: OAuth token endpoint at /api/v4/oauth/token. Scopes are read and forecast. No public signup was found.
sources.official: Yes, official commercial feed. DDHQ is an independent decision desk.

sources.name: Kalshi public market-data API
sources.latency: Near real time. Prices move as traders react to returns. Docs also advertise websockets, which I did not probe.
sources.granularity: National and race-level only. It carries odds, not vote counts. Examples: CONTROLH-2026 (House control) and per-race markets.
sources.verified_live: YES. GET /markets?event_ticker=CONTROLH-2026 returned JSON, HTTP 200, no key. The Democratic House contract showed last_price 0.97 in my probe. The events endpoint returned CONTROLH-2026 with last_updated_ts 2026-10-28.
sources.notes: This is a proxy signal, not results. It is useful as a live implied-probability overlay on a dashboard. Trading requires an account, but reads do not.
sources.official: Official public API from a regulated exchange

sources.name: Polymarket Gamma API
sources.latency: Near real time for prices. Gamma is a metadata and price snapshot layer; the CLOB API and websocket give live order books.
sources.granularity: National and race-level odds only. No vote counts.
sources.verified_live: YES. /events returned JSON, HTTP 200, no key. The slug which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026 (id 32225) resolves. A search for house control returned a market on the November 2 favorite.
sources.notes: Same use as Kalshi: a probability overlay, not results. Some markets resolve against third-party sources, so read each market's rules. Polymarket access may be geo-restricted for trading, but reads worked from here.

sources.name: Cicero (Azavea/Cicero Data)
sources.cost: API credits at roughly $40 minimum purchase. Bulk packages run from about $298 up to about $8,848 (list vs discounted tiers, e.g. $298/$268). One credit equals one address matched to districts and officials. These are credit-pack prices and I did not map each price to a credit count.
sources.latency: Not applicable. This is not an election results feed.
sources.granularity: Address to district and elected official lookup.
sources.verified_live: Site returns HTTP 200 and the pricing page loaded.
sources.notes: Useful only for a lookup feature, such as an address to its districts and candidates. It does not provide results.

sources.name: Ballotpedia API
sources.cost: Not confirmed. I did not find a published price.
sources.latency: Not a live results feed. Ballotpedia publishes results after the fact on its wiki pages.
sources.granularity: Candidates, districts, and races. Results lag.
sources.verified_live: Not confirmed. My curl loop failed before this URL was probed, and api.ballotpedia.org was not checked either.
sources.notes: Treat as unverified. It is more of a candidate and ballot data product than a live count feed.

sources.name: Reuters / Edison Research
sources.cost: Not researched. These are enterprise feeds sold to media organizations. No public pricing was found, and I did not search further.
sources.verified_live: NO. I did not probe these.
sources.notes: Almost certainly not available to an individual on election night. I ran no searches for this or for Clarity/Civix, RapidAPI, or other cheap resellers, so those are gaps in my slice. The Clarity/Civix item is also the Clarity Elections (SOE) per-county results feed, which could cover some counties but was not checked.

summary:
Short version: there is no cheap, self-serve, real-time paid results API that an individual can buy tonight. The two real commercial feeds, AP and Decision Desk HQ, are both sales-gated with no published prices. The only live APIs I could probe and use right now are the free Kalshi and Polymarket market APIs. They give odds, not vote counts.

What I verified with curl tonight:
- Kalshi: https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets?event_ticker=CONTROLH-2026 returned JSON with HTTP 200 and no key. The Democratic House contract showed last_price 0.97.
- Polymarket: https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/events returned JSON with HTTP 200 and no key. The slug which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026 resolves.
- AP: the developer portal loads, but api.ap.org/v2/elections returned 403 without a key.
- DDHQ: the docs site loads. The API needs OAuth credentials that I could not obtain.

What I could not confirm:
- No AP or DDHQ prices. Both appear to be contact-sales only.
- Whether DDHQ has any hobbyist tier. I found none.
- Update latency for AP and DDHQ was not stated in anything I could read.
- Reuters/Edison, Clarity/Civix, Ballotpedia, RapidAPI listings, and other cheap resellers were not searched or probed, so my slice is incomplete there. Another agent should cover county-level sources such as Clarity/SOE feeds and the Dutchess County BOE.

Dashboard implication: prediction-market odds plus any free official or state/county feeds from other slices are the realistic route tonight. Paid AP or DDHQ access would need a sales conversation and is unlikely to be granted to an individual in time.
